THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 07.11.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 M.A.C.A.No.2434 of 2014 3  2025:KER:84809  JUDGMENT  This appeal is filed by the third  respondent/insurer in O.P.(MV) No.86 of 2007 on the The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Lalitha P.V on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148994886/
2  files of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Pathanamthitta, challenging their liability to pay the award amount as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondents herein are the petitioners and respondents 1 and 2 before the tribunal.

2. Brief facts of the case are as follows :-
On 01.12.2006, while the deceased Raju was walking along the road, a Tata Sumo bearing registration No. KL-03/K- 306, driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit him, as a result of which he sustained fatal injuries.
Later he succumbed to the injuries.

The claimants who are the legal heirs of the deceased,
approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 8,00,250/-.
3. The first respondent was the driver of the 2025:KER:84809 offending vehicle and the second respondent was its owner, before the tribunal.

The third respondent insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy of the said vehicle, but disputing the alleged negligence and the quantum of compensation claimed and also denied their liability for violation of policy condition by contending that the 1st respondent has no valid driving licence at the time of the alleged accident.
Exts.A1 to A9 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record,
awarded a sum of 7,58,378/- as compensation under different heads with interest @9% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from the respondent therein.
Challenging the liability and quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the third respondent/insurance company has come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned standing counsel for the appellant insurer and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents.

The learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the driver of the Tata Sumo involved in the accident was not having a valid driving licence at the time of the alleged incident but the tribunal has not granted the right to recover the amount from the owner of the vehicle.
After filing of the appeal, notice was issued to the 5 th respondent herein, the owner of the vehicle.
Thereafter, the legal heirs of the 5th respondent filed a petition to implead themselves in the party array, since the 5th respondent was no more.
In the said application, it was contended that the 5th respondent had died even prior to the passing of the award.

It was also submitted that the driver of the vehicle possessed a valid driving licence at the time of the accident, and Annexure A2, a copy of the driving licence of the 4th respondent, was produced in support of the same.
The learned Standing Counsel further submitted that the licence of the 4th respondent was verified by them and found that the driving licence 2025:KER:84809 was valid at the time of the accident.
Hence the contention that there was no valid driving licence does not stand and the insurer is not entitled to claim right of recovery.

Though the 5th respondent expired even prior to the passing of the award,

sentences.text:
The appellant challenges the compensation mainly under the following heads:
Compensation for loss of dependency :-

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted that the main ground raised in the appeal is that instead of 10%, the tribunal has added 15% future prospects to the income fixed.
I find force in the argument.
The deceased person was a toddy tapper and was aged 52 years.
Hence the addition to be made towards future prospects is 10%, and not 15%.
The Tribunal had fixed the income of the deceased as 4,000/-.
I find 2025:KER:84809

that , going by the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the monthly income of the deceased is refixed as 5,500/- per month for an accident that occured in the year 2006.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further adding 10% future prospects
to the income fixed
, the monthly income is 6,050/- for the purpose of calculating dependency.

Although, it is true that the claimant has not filed any appeal or cross-objection challenging the quantum of compensation, considering that the Act is a beneficial legislation and in order to ensure just and reasonable compensation, I find it appropriate to refix the income.

Accordingly, following the apex court judgments in National Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)], and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)], the compensation payable under the said head is recalculated as thus:
5,32,400/- (6,050x12x11x2/3).

sentences.text: The tribunal has already paid an amount of 4,04,800/- under the said head.
Thus, 2025:KER:84809 there will be an additional amount of 1,27,600/- under the head loss of dependency.
Compensation for loss of consortium/Loss of love and affection :- On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the tribunal has awarded an amount of 1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium.

Considering the fact that there are three legal heirs, going by the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), I find that the claimants are entitled for a total amount of 1,20,000/- (40,000x3) towards loss of consortium.
Therefore, the appellants are entitled to get an additional compensation of 20,000/- under the head loss of consortium.

7. The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance submitted that the tribunal has awarded an amount of 2,00,000/- towards loss of love and affection, which is against the principle laid down in the judgment in New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 (5) KLT OnLine 1198 (SC)], wherein it has been held that once compensation is awarded under the head loss of 2025:KER:84809 consortium, no amount shall be awarded under the head loss of love and affection, as it would amount to duplication of compensation.

sentences.text: Hence I am inclined to delete 2,00,000/- awarded under the said head.

sentences.text: Compensation for funeral expenses/Compensation for estate :- The learned standing counsel for the insurance company submits that the tribunal has awarded an amount of 25,000/- as compensation towards funeral expenses.
Following the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), the compensation under the conventional heads ought to have been fixed at 15,000/- only.
Whereas, the learned counsel for the claimants submits that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 5,000/- as compensation towards funeral expenses.
Following the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), the compensation under both the conventional heads ought to have been fixed at 30,000/- together.

Accordingly, since it is seen that the tribunal has awarded 5,000/- and 25,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses together, totalling to 30,000/-, I 2025:KER:84809 do not find any reason to interfere with the same.

8. Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:

Bystander's 3,000 1,000 (not 1,000 expenses modified) 6 Damage to clothes 1,000 1,000 (not 1,000 modified)

7 Medical expenses 23,000 5,578 (not 5,578 modified) 8 Funeral expenses 40,000 25,000 (not 30,000 9 Loss of estate 50,000 5,000 modified) 10 Pain and 50,000 10,000 (not 10,000 sufferings modified) 11 Loss of love and affection 1,50,000 2,00,000 2,00,000 Deleted (-) 2025:KER:84809 12 Loss of 1,50,000 1,00,000 20,000 1,20,000

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and the claimants are awarded a total amount of 7,05,978/-
(Rupees Seven lakhs five thousand nine hundred and seventy eight only) as compensation under different heads after reducing an amount of 52,400/- from the impugned award with interest @9%
per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.
The appellant insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimants shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the appellant insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the appellant insurer to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall 2025:KER:84809 be open for the appellant insurer to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the claimants at the earliest in accordance with law.
The ratio adopted by the tribunal shall be followed in respect of the enhanced compensation as well.
